item.title: Clippers Exercise 1st-Rounder’s Option Despite Long-Term Injury
item.description: Support Local Media - Click to Add LA Sports Report as a Preferred Source on Google The Los Angeles Clippers picked up center Yanic Konan Niederhauser’s third-year team option during his recovery from surgery on his foot. Source: The LA Clippers are picking up Yanic Konan Niederhauser’s third year team option. — Jake Fischer (@JakeLFischer) October 29, 2026 Niederhauser suffered his foot injury towards the end of last season, tearing his Lisfranc ligament to end his rookie season early. The injury cost him his offseason and preseason, but he is likely to return fairly soon. The Clippers drafted Niederhauser in the first round of the 2025 NBA Draft, and he saw the floor 41 times in his rookie season in a limited role. He averaged 10.3 minutes per game last season, posting 4.3 points and 2.9 rebounds per game. The 6-foot-11 big man scored 10 or ore points in seven appearances last year, playing more than 20 minutes in six of those games. Mar 1, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Clippers center Yanic Konan Niederhauser (14) reacts after dunks the ball during the second half against the New Orleans Pelicans at Intuit Dome. Mandatory Credit: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images What Will Yanic Konan Niederhauser’s Role Look Like When He Comes Back? While the Clippers clearly have their eyes on Niederhauser, he probably won’t command a huge role when he returns to action. The Clippers have two serviceable NBA centers in Brook Lopez and Isaiah Jackson, both of whom are averaging more than 20 minutes per game on the year. Lopez has been especially impressive in his age-38 season, averaging 14 points per game with 4.8 rebounds. Rookie Baba Miller, who the Clippers selected in the second round of the most recent draft, is also getting some playing time, playing a similar role to Niederhauser before his injury last season. Miller is averaging 3.0 rebounds and 2.7 points per game in 9.7 minutes per night. That being said, Niederhauser could still be important part to the team when he returns. The Clippers have struggled grabbing boards so far this season, ranking 27th in the league in rebounding through their first four games of the season. Adding a presence like Niederhauser in the paint could help them in that area and give the second-year player some increased opportunity. Niederhauser didn’t join the Clippers on their two-game road trip, as the team prioritized his recovery over travel, but they’ll hope to have some good news regarding his status when they return. Their next game comes against the Minnesota Timberwolves in their first game of the 2026-27 NBA Cup on Friday at 5:00 p.m. PT. item.title: Eintracht Frankfurt restructure sporting department after Krösche's exit
item.description: Eintracht Frankfurt restructure sporting department after Krösche's exit Following Markus Krösche’s departure as board member for sport earlier this month, Eintracht Frankfurt have reshuffled responsibilities within their sporting department. With the club yet to appoint Krösche’s successor, sporting director Timmu Hardung will assume increased responsibility and work closely with CEO Axel Hellmann to improve efficiency across the department and oversee preparations for the winter transfer window. As a result, Hardung will put his day-to-day duties involving the squad and coaching staff on hold. Former Eintracht player Sebastian Rode, who is currently completing a trainee programme at the club, will take on greater responsibility within the first-team setup. “In this current period until the appointment of a new board member for sport, we want to consolidate responsibilities and improve the efficiency of work across the various departments," said club CEO Axel Hellmann. "Timmo Hardung has been tasked, until further notice, with leading all sporting operations in men’s football. The expansion of his responsibilities means that the focus of his work must shift from the team to strategic and organisational matters. Timmo Hardung will therefore, in close consultation with myself, focus more heavily on processes and structures. "At the same time, we want to provide the best possible support for day-to-day work within the immediate team environment. As a highly respected former player, Sebastian Rode brings valuable qualities to this role through his experience, his personality and his close ties to Eintracht. As part of his trainee programme, he can contribute this perspective while also gaining further experience within the sporting organisation.” Joti Chatzialexiou, sporting managing director at 1. FC Nürnberg, has emerged as the leading candidate to succeed Krösche, with Sky reporting that Eintracht have reached an agreement with him on personal terms. Should Eintracht Frankfurt’s supervisory board approve Chatzialexiou’s appointment, the club would then need to open negotiations with Nürnberg.

item.title: Davenport jiu-jitsu community brings together beginners, families and a 61-year-old black belt
item.description: Students watch a technique demonstration during a class at Gracie Barra Davenport. Owner Fillipe Pascalicchio says the academy introduced a women-only class about a month ago. Gracie Barra Davenport Bill Mason discovered Brazilian jiu-jitsu when his striking instructor wasn’t available one day. He tried a different class and found himself hooked. Now 61 and a black belt, Mason says the training has given him much more than techniques. “What keeps me going is a lot of things: the camaraderie, the sense of community, the trust you build with people, and the fact that you’re always evolving,” Mason said in written responses shared with Channel 9 by Gracie Barra Davenport . Academy owner Fillipe Pascalicchio says that sense of connection is drawing people who have no plans to compete, including parents, children and adults trying martial arts for the first time. A physical puzzle Pascalicchio describes Brazilian jiu-jitsu as a martial art focused on leverage, positioning and technique. Much of the training takes place on the ground, with partners working to establish control and apply submissions such as joint locks or chokes. Unlike boxing or kickboxing, the training he describes does not involve punches or kicks. “In class it feels like solving a physical puzzle with a partner,” Pascalicchio said. He estimates about 98% of his students are hobbyists rather than competitors. Some parents begin training after bringing their children to classes, while other adults arrive looking for exercise or self-defense instruction, he said. A new class for women Pascalicchio said the academy introduced a women-only class about a month ago after receiving more inquiries from women interested in training in a comfortable setting. The academy now has more than 30 women training overall, he said. For children, Pascalicchio emphasizes discipline, confidence and responding to bullying. For adults, he points to the physical challenge, concentration and friendships that develop through regular practice. Classes are divided by age and experience level, he said. Beginners start with fundamentals and practice techniques slowly with a partner before progressing. Adapting through setbacks Mason said his path included recovering from a serious bike accident that left his left hand shattered. “It took me a year before I could lift a gallon of milk,” he said. “It took me a long time to figure out how to do things again. It was a learning curve every single day.” He said a separate hockey accident later cost him his thumb. Mason began jiu-jitsu at 43. Earning his black belt, awarded just over a year ago according to Pascalicchio, fulfilled a longtime goal. “I was totally surprised when I got my black belt. item.title: Big 12 Hits UCF With $100,000 Fine Over Offensive Fan Chants in BYU Matchup
item.description: UCF pulled off a massive overtime win against No. 2 BYU, but UCF has suffered a tough decision against them from the Big 12. UCF celebrated but used chants that was not taken well by the conference. The Big 12 acted fast and let UCF taste the consequences of the misconduct by their fans. UCF counts massive fines from Big 12 On October 24, 2026, UCF hosted then-ranked No. 2 BYU in a Big 12 football game at Acrisure Bounce House in Orlando. The Knights staged a major upset, winning 39-31 in overtime. During the game, groups of UCF fans—particularly in the student section repeatedly chanted vulgar anti-LDS slogans. “F*** the Mormons,” that’s the chant that got UCF in trouble. Jul 12, 2023; Arlington, TX, USA; A view of the UCF Knights helmet and logo during Big 12 football media day at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-USA TODAY Sports Four days later, the Big 12 Conference fined UCF $100,000 for the discriminatory conduct. The money is designated for student education initiatives. At the same time, the league introduced a stricter policy. A first confirmed incident now carries an automatic $100,000 fine, and a second incident in the same game can trigger an in-game competitive penalty such as a 15-yard unsportsmanlike-conduct foul plus possible additional fines. The issue is treated as serious because it goes beyond typical sports trash talk. The chants targeted the religious identity of BYU, which is owned and operated by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Stadium officials issued multiple warnings over the public-address system and removed some fans, but the chants continued. Similar anti-LDS chants have occurred at multiple Big 12 venues in recent seasons, leading to previous fines against other schools. Other schools paid fines for similar incidents On September 27, 2025, BYU played at Colorado’s Folsom Field and won a close 24-21 game. During the contest, fans in the Colorado student section repeatedly chanted “F*** BYU” and “F*** the Mormons.” Three days later, the Big 12 Conference issued Colorado a public reprimand and a $50,000 fine. On February 4, 2026, Oklahoma State hosted BYU in Stillwater and won 99-92. Late in the game, the student section was heard chanting “F*** the Mormons” BYU coach Kevin Young publicly addressed the chants afterward. “There was some ‘F the Mormons’ chants tonight by the student section that I heard. It’s a great win for Oklahoma State University. Their fans should be proud. But it would be great if some class was in there as well.” Young said . The Big 12 investigated and, a few days later, fined Oklahoma State $50,000. The school accepted the penalty without appeal. These two cases were the most recent Big 12 fines for anti-LDS chants before the larger $100,000 penalty against UCF in October 2026. item.description: Avery Johnson and the Kansas State Wildcats are not having a good 2026 season. They are having quite a disappointing season under first-year head coach Collin Klein. The college football program has an overall 4–3 record, but only 1–3 in the Big 12. Already suffering with the results, the program has been hit with another devastating news. One key player will not be able to play in an upcoming crucial fixture. Avery Johnson “unlikely to play” against Colorado Buffs Kansas State starting quarterback Johnson has been officially ruled out for the Wildcats’’ October 31, 2026, game against the Colorado Buffs at Folsom Field. The team confirmed the news in their latest availability report. This marks the second consecutive contest he will miss after sitting out the previous week’s 28-17 loss at Arizona State. Oct 21, 2023; Manhattan, Kansas, USA; Kansas State Wildcats quarterback Avery Johnson (5) warms up before the start of a game against the TCU Horned Frogs at Bill Snyder Family Football Stadium. The Wildcats completed their season with a win in the Pop-Tarts Bowl, 28-19. Mandatory Credit: Scott Sewell-USA TODAY Sports The injury originated in the first quarter of Kansas State’s October 17 victory over the Kansas Jayhawks. Johnson broke free for a 59-yard run, fell awkwardly to the turf, and remained down for several minutes receiving medical attention. He missed only one play, returned to finish the game, and showed no immediate lingering issues on the field. However, effects from the play, described by multiple reports as involving the neck/shoulder area persisted, leading coach Collin Klein to keep details private to protect the player’s medical confidentiality. Klein had previously labeled Johnson day-to-day, noting that any return depended on the speed of his recovery process under the guidance of the team’s medical staff. Johnson had started 32 consecutive games prior to the Arizona State absence and entered the season as a productive dual-threat option, completing 118 of 187 passes for 1,301 yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions while adding 462 rushing yards and three scores. To add further complications, backup quarterback Jacob Knuth, who started against Arizona State and completed 26 of 41 passes for 194 yards and a touchdown while adding a rushing score, is also listed as doubtful after rolling his ankle twice in that game. Kansas State may turn to Blake Barnett or Dillon Duff instead. Klein said about the situation, “I don’t know exactly who is going to take the first snap on Saturday. That is where we’re at.” It remains to be seen what steps the program will take next. item.title: Dream beat Valkyries to force WNBA Finals decider after tipoff time backlash
item.description: Allisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard added 21 as the sharp-shooting Atlanta Dream staved off a late Golden State Valkyries rally to claim an 80-69 victory in Game 6 on Thursday, drawing level in the WNBA Finals. A decisive Game 7 will take place at Golden State on Saturday night, with both franchises competing to secure their first WNBA championship. After suffering their lowest scoring games of the Finals in back-to-back losses in Games 4 and 5, the Dream delivered an offensive revival when confronted with a must-win situation. On Wednesday, the Dream announced a sellout crowd for Game 6 despite criticism of the 12:30pm EDT tipoff. Concerns over work and school obligations hurting attendance proved largely unfounded, with only scattered empty seats in the upper level. Angel Reese recorded a double-double with 15 points and 13 rebounds for Atlanta. Gabby Williams paced the Valkyries with 26 points, while Tiffany Hayes added 15. Atlanta held a lead as large as 25 points before the Valkyries mounted a furious late charge, cutting the margin to 77-66 on two free throws by Laeticia Amihere with 1:57 remaining. Angel Reese starred for Atlanta (Getty) Having been restricted to just 22 points in the first half of their 65-55 defeat in Game 5, the Dream matched that total within the opening 6:30 of the first quarter. 3-pointers provided much of the early momentum. Atlanta made 6 of 8 shots from beyond the arc and shot 11 of 15 overall while building a 32-15 lead in the opening period. Leading 6-5, the Dream broke the game open with a 13-0 run that featured a pair of 3-pointers from Jordin Canada. Reese joined the perimeter display by sinking a 3-pointer from the corner in the second quarter. Prior to the game, Atlanta boasted a perfect 15-0 record when Reese hit at least one 3-pointer. Atlanta maintained its clinical shooting to establish a 46-26 halftime lead, while Golden State struggled to find rhythm. The Valkyries made only 9 of 34 shots in the half against Atlanta’s relentless defense. Howard started the second half with another 3-pointer. Valkyries guard Veronica Burton was called for a flagrant foul midway through the third quarter after an officials’ review determined she made unnecessary windup and contact on Howard’s face during a drive. Kaila Charles closed the third quarter with a 3-pointer for Golden State to reduce Atlanta’s lead to 16 points at 63-47. It marked the Dream’s smallest advantage since their first-quarter spurt. Golden State pulled within 13 points at 68-55 before Gray and Reese hit 3-pointers to push the gap to 74-55. Williams cut the deficit to 77-69 before Gray delivered a crucial 3-pointer for Atlanta. Hayes received her fifth foul during a collision for a loose ball with 5:01 left. She departed the court slowly after being attended to by a trainer.

item.description: Barcelona temporarily close supporters’ cheering section after El Clasico incidents Barcelona are preparing for an important week following consecutive defeats against PSG and Real Madrid. Hansi Flick’s side will be desperate to return to winning ways. They face Deportivo Alaves at home this weekend in a crucial game for the Catalans. Now, Barça will have to face Alaves without the organised support of one of their most vocal fan groups. Barcelona’s board has decided to temporarily suspend the operation of Gol 1957 for Saturday’s league encounter. The club confirmed the decision following a series of disciplinary proceedings involving supporters in the aftermath of the Clasico . “FC Barcelona has decided to suspend the operation of Gol 1957, known as the supporters’ section , for the next league match against Alaves,” the statement read. Barcelona take action following Clasico controversy The decision follows several incidents during the Real Madrid clash that attracted attention and have now led to disciplinary scrutiny. Eduardo Camavinga was struck with a pole at the Camp Nou. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images) La Liga documented 17 incidents from the Clasico , including 10 involving Barcelona supporters. These included offensive chants directed at Marc Cucurella and Jose Mourinho. Objects were thrown onto the pitch during Real Madrid’s celebrations. One supporter from Gol 1957 was also identified following an incident in which Eduardo Camavinga was struck with a flag. Barcelona have explained that the repeated disciplinary proceedings could expose the club to financial penalties or even the possibility of a stadium closure. Barcelona hoping to reopen section against Aston Villa Importantly, the suspension is intended to be temporary rather than a permanent closure of the organised supporters’ section. The club plans to meet representatives of the different groups within Gol 1957 over the coming days to establish clear commitments regarding acceptable behaviour. item.title: LeBron James looked all 41 years of his life on these highlight plays
item.description: LeBron James is essentially outlasting every elite athlete in the history of sports by playing his 24th season for the Philadelphia 76ers this year. James turns 42 years old in Dec., and if he fulfills the second year of his contract next season, he will have played 10 more seasons than Michael Jordan. James’ peak wasn’t as high as MJ’s by most models , but he’s trying to win the GOAT debate on longevity, and he’s certainly made it a worthwhile discussion. Father Time doesn’t lose, and that’s even the case against a freak of nature like LeBron. James showed some signs of age on Wednesday night as his 76ers needed a big fourth quarter comeback just to get by the Indiana Pacers without Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac. James was solid in the win with 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds, and three stocks, but he was also on the wrong end of two highlight plays that the internet is still talking about a day later. Early in the second quarter, James was speeding down the court for what should have been a fastbreak dunk. Instead, Indiana’s Jalen Slawson, who is only on a two-way contract, beat him to the rim for the chasedown block. He did a LeBron to LeBron! Watch the play here: JALEN SLAWSON CHASEDOWN BLOCK 😤 pic.twitter.com/OMB0kg8squ — Indiana Pacers (@Pacers) October 28, 2026 LeBron was never caught from behind for years and years and years. There’s only so much he can do before he turns 42, though, and this time another super athlete like Slawson got the best of him. Look at Slawson talk trash to LeBron at the end of that clip. Have some respect for your elders, young man! I say this as a big Slawson fan, he was on my ‘too good for Summer League’ list this year. As if that wasn’t ba enough, LeBron got got even worse late in the fourth quarter. Pacers guard Andrew Nembhard squared up James and hit him with a dirty crossover that sent the 40-something tumbling. Nembhard missed the shot, so this clip isn’t as humiliating as it could have been. NEMBHARD ANKLE BREAKER ON LEBRON 😭 pic.twitter.com/FQIjF5Gi57 — Basketball Performances (@NBAPerformances) October 29, 2026 The Sixers came back and won to improve to 4-1 on the year. That’s great. LeBron has stayed durable while so many other players have gone down with injuries early this season, and he’s poised to be a key piece of a team with championship aspirations come playoff time. Everything LeBron is doing at this age is crazy, but he’s still showing plenty of signs of slowing down. The end is near, but LeBron is fighting for his athletic life unlike anyone we’ve ever seen before.

item.description: Pat McAfee revealed Wednesday that there have been death threats against him as a result of the controversey surrouding ESPN’s “College GameDay” visit to Utah. “I’ve stayed away from my mentions and DMs this month since these back to back days but ... I’m sure if I went in there now, I’d find some wishes for and threats of death for me,” McAfee poated on X. “‘Don’t read them.’ They’re everywhere.” The post includes screenshots from direct messages threatening violence against him and tweets expressing a desire to see him dead. McAfee said he felt “uncomfortable” after the University of Utah posted a since-deleted video of students “dogging” him. He also said the video shared by the university account was inciteful against him. McAfee cited the visit to the University of Utah reminded him of assassination of Charlie Kirk . Utah, for its part, apologized Monday. “I do get a bit (expletive) up when a couple days after The New York Times releases a ‘WE ARE ALLOWED TO AND SHOULD HATE THIS GUY’ piece, a university puts a video out from their own page, indicating, ‘We think he’s a corny creep here.’ It’s a weird time,” McAfee posted. “The things that get said about what my daughter and son and wife deserve are all rather wild as well.” McAfee cited an experience ahead of “College GameDay” in Knoxville, Tennessee, in 2025 — the show’s first episode after Kirk was killed. He said security concerns arose about a potential “copycat” scenario, as “GameDay” was “the next huge gathering on a campus.” He claimed FBI snipers and a “huge” police presence were on hand to ensure the safety of “GameDay,” adding that it was suggested to him to wear a bulletproof vest. “The world, in front of the entire internet, just proved that we had gotten to a rather extreme place,” McAfee posted. “How’d we get here? I had to wrestle with that a bit. FBI’s sending snipers so me and the lads don’t get shot. That’s crazy. item.title: Should I Start Bryce Young? Week 8 Fantasy Football Outlook for Panthers QB
item.description: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - OCTOBER 25: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers looks on before a football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Bank of America Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Thursday Night Football always seems to bring with it some extra difficult fantasy football lineup decisions. Like, for example, whether you should start or sit Carolina Panthers QB Bryce Young in Week 8 against the Green Bay Packers. The Panthers are going to Lambeau Field hoping to rebound from a disaster against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Carolina is also shorthanded due to injuries, although that looks like it’ll impact the defense more than the offense. It’s worth noting that the Panthers’ offensive line is far from full strength, though. So that brings us to Young. He’s had a stronger passing season than just about anyone expected. But at Lambeau on Thursday, can you trust him? Should I Start Bryce Young? Our instincts say, just barely, that starting Young is risky business and he may be worth sitting on Thursday night. This all depends on your league size and format, of course. Young is a starter in any 2-QB or Superflex leagues, no question. But in a standard league where you start one quarterback, with 10 or 12 teams in your league, Young might be just on the outside looking in. Bryce Young Fantasy Ranking Week 8 ESPN’s Week 8 rankings align with Young being right on the border. They rank him as their No. 11 QB for the week. That includes a ranking as high as No. 9 from one of their analysts and a ranking as low as No. 14 from another. It averages out to the 11th spot. Of course, this isn’t done in a vacuum. It all depends on whether you have a better option than Young. The 10 players ESPN lists ahead of Young are Josh Allen, Drake Maye, Joe Burrow, Lamar Jackson, Jayden Daniels, Trevor Lawrence, Dak Prescott, Jordan Love, Matthew Stafford and Geno Smith. The likes of Kyler Murray, Kirk Cousins and even Caleb Williams, Baker Mayfield and Patrick Mahomes are behind Young. Even in tough matchups, it’d be tough to sit Caleb or Baker and play Young. Packers Defense The Packers have had a solid pass defense this season. They’ve allowed the 21st-most passing yards (meaning they’re in the better half of the league as far as pass defense). They’ve also allowed just nine TD passes in seven games, and they’ve also intercepted nine passes. It’s tough to justify starting Young against a defense with those numbers that will be at home in a primetime game. If your other QB is on a bye this week — potentially Brock Purdy or C.J. Stroud, or even J.J. McCarthy or Tyler Shough — then you can feel OK about Young. But in a one-QB league, there’s a chance it’s another rough day at the office for Young.
